researcher_notes: Coverage is bimodal, similar to the POS and Payments passes: Paytronix and Thanx (both actively press-release/case-study their named restaurant wins) yielded strong benches of 7-8 dated records each, reusing and independently re-verifying URLs already indexed in the 2026-07-21 research archive (archive_registry had crawled both vendors -- 194 raw candidate_evidence rows for Paytronix, 75 for Thanx). PAR Punchh (part of PAR Technology Corp, ticker PAR) also came back solid with 3 records including a 2025 SEC/earnings-adjacent brand-wide win (Torchy's Tacos) and a large enterprise account (CKE Restaurants / Carl's Jr. & Hardee's). SevenRooms and Bikky, both younger/adjacent guest-data platforms, produced usable dated evidence (SevenRooms: ThinkFoodGroup, Marriott; Bikky: City Barbeque, Blaze Pizza, Eggs Up Grill). The remaining seven vendors were thin or required significant corrections to the task's assumed corporate structure: (1) SessionM was acquired by Mastercard in 2019 and is NOT still an independent brand -- as of an April 2026 announcement it is being divested again, this time to Capillary Technologies, so 'SessionM (Mastercard)' is now mid-transition to a third owner; only one named restaurant client (Chipotle, via a 2019 trade-press client list, not a dedicated case study) was found. (2) Fivestars was NOT acquired by Sunbit as the task brief assumed -- it was acquired by SumUp in October 2021 for $317M and no Sunbit transaction was found in any source; this is flagged as a correction, and Fivestars evidence came back thin regardless (only small independent shops, no named multi-unit restaurant chain with a date). (3) LevelUp (Grubhub) is a genuinely historical/legacy relationship set, not a current one: the standalone LevelUp consumer app was discontinued September 30, 2021, its tech was folded into Grubhub's restaurant-facing products, and Grubhub itself was sold by Just Eat Takeaway to Wonder Group in a deal that closed January 2025 -- so 'LevelUp' today is two ownership changes removed from the 2013-2018 relationships found (Sweetgreen, Pret A Manger) and those are recorded as discontinued_or_replaced/legacy_incumbent. (4) Yumpingo was acquired by Black Box Intelligence on April 28, 2025 and its case-study URLs now 301-redirect into BBI's site/brand (BBI Survey Studio); only one solid dated relationship (Rosa Mexicano, 2019) was independently confirmed, a second (The Restaurant Group / Chiquito / Frankie & Benny's) exists only as an undated marketing reference and could not be independently dated or re-confirmed post-acquisition. (5) Fishbowl went through a rename (Personica -> Fishbowl, 2023) and was itself just acquired by GoTab (announced June 9, 2026) -- no dated, named restaurant-chain case study was found despite extensive searching; the one case study located does not name the restaurant group. (6) Como (Como Sense) came back with no verifiable primary-source evidence at all -- secondary aggregator/blog sources claim Burger King and Quiznos as Como customers, but a direct search of Burger King's own newsroom and loyalty coverage found only its own 'Royal Perks' program with no vendor attribution to Como, which is exactly the task's flagged failure mode (consumer-facing program name vs. underlying vendor); this claim is NOT included as a record and Como is treated as unverified/thin. (7) Kangaroo Rewards and Craver both came back essentially empty for named, dated multi-unit restaurant chains as expected for smaller regional players -- Craver's only identifiable example (Rook Coffee, a small NJ coffee chain) is included as a single Low-confidence record; Kangaroo Rewards produced no usable named-brand evidence whatsoever. Preferred Patron produced exactly one strong dated record (Happy Lemon USA, a 135-store bubble tea franchise, July 2025 press release) and nothing else confirmable. A methodology note: several 'Relationship candidate' rows in the 2026-07-21 archive for both Paytronix and Thanx were mis-tagged 'Pizza Press, The' / 'Stand Restaurants, The' / 'Taco Stand, The' due to fuzzy string matching against unrelated press releases (e.g. Paytronix-Deliverect, Paytronix-mParticle, Paytronix-Qu partnership announcements) -- these were not carried forward as records for those brands. Separately, dozens of 'Mention candidate' rows for both vendors (McDonald's, Chick-fil-A, Dunkin', Domino's, Pizza Hut, Buffalo Wild Wings, Red Robin, Checkers, Starbucks, Taco Bell, Chipotle) turned out on inspection to be Paytronix/Thanx blog posts analyzing competitors' loyalty programs, not vendor relationships -- these are exactly the failure mode flagged in the task instructions and were excluded entirely.

vendors_with_thin_or_no_evidence: Fishbowl -- despite extensive searching (own press page, FeaturedCustomers aggregator, blog/guides), no dated press release or case study naming a specific, identifiable restaurant brand/chain customer was found. One case study describes 'a Peruvian-inspired restaurant group with two prominent establishments in New York City' via a Resy partnership, but does not name the operator. Fishbowl's own marketing claims '50,000+ restaurants' served in aggregate, with no individual named/dated wins located.

Como (Como Sense) -- no primary-source press release or case study naming any specific restaurant brand was found at all. Secondary/aggregator blog content (revolttek.com, backofhouse.io) claims Burger King and Quiznos as Como customers, but a direct check of Burger King's own newsroom and loyalty program coverage found no vendor attribution to Como (only Burger King's own 'Royal Perks' program name) -- this looks like exactly the task-flagged failure mode of conflating a brand's own program name with an unconfirmed underlying vendor, so it was not included as a record.

Kangaroo Rewards -- extensive searching turned up only generic marketing copy ('hundreds of restaurants, cafes and bars') and unnamed customer testimonials; no dated press release or case study naming any specific restaurant chain was found.

Fivestars -- despite being a long-established loyalty platform (founded 2011, 14,000+ merchants claimed), no dated press release or case study naming a specific multi-unit restaurant chain was found. Named examples that do exist (Armadillo Willy's, an 8-store BBQ chain; Soulman's BBQ; Verde Tea Cafe) are small, mostly single-market operators without confirmable dates.
vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_r: SessionM (Mastercard) -- acquired by Mastercard in October 2019; as of an April 2026 announcement, Capillary Technologies has a definitive agreement to acquire SessionM from Mastercard, a second ownership change. Platform still appears to be actively maintained (2025.4 release notes dated October 2025 were found), but its branding/ownership is mid-transition and 'SessionM (Mastercard)' will likely be inaccurate within the graph's normal update cycle.

Fivestars (Sunbit) -- CORRECTION to the task brief's assumption: Fivestars was acquired by SumUp in October 2021 for approximately $317M, not by Sunbit. No Sunbit-Fivestars transaction was found in any source searched. Fivestars continues to operate under the SumUp umbrella as of this research date; recommend Todd update the vendor universe label from 'Fivestars (Sunbit)' to 'Fivestars (SumUp)' or similar.

LevelUp (Grubhub) -- the standalone LevelUp consumer app was discontinued September 30, 2021 (not merely renamed); its technology was folded into Grubhub's restaurant-facing product line (e.g. Grubhub Direct). Grubhub itself changed ownership in a deal that closed January 2025, sold by Just Eat Takeaway to Wonder Group for $650M. Any 'LevelUp' relationship evidence found is therefore historical/legacy by definition -- both records included in this batch (Pret A Manger 2018, sweetgreen 2013) predate the 2018 Grubhub acquisition and are scored discontinued_or_replaced/legacy_incumbent accordingly.

Yumpingo -- acquired by Black Box Intelligence on April 28, 2025 (the seventh exit for investor Branded Hospitality Ventures). Yumpingo's own case-study URLs now 301-redirect into Black Box Intelligence's domain/brand (some redirecting further into 'BBI Survey Studio' branding), and at least one previously-existing case study (The Restaurant Group) could not be re-located at its redirected destination. Recommend treating 'Yumpingo' as a historical/absorbed brand going forward rather than a fully independent vendor.

Fishbowl -- underwent a rename from 'Personica' back to 'Fishbowl' in April 2023, and was itself acquired by GoTab (a restaurant commerce platform) in an acquisition announced June 9, 2026 -- meaning Fishbowl is a very recently-absorbed brand as of this research date, layered on top of the earlier Personica rename.
